messages:
Priya R.: legal pinged — DSAR came in with a notarized PDF signed under a key that rotated last month. they want verifiable proof-of-deletion + chain-of-custody. any red flags?
Miguel T.: we follow minimization: we don't keep raw uploads in app DB. we store evidence_ref -> S3 + metadata. during DSAR processing we copy to secure bucket and re-encrypt with our CMK (redwood-dsar-keystore).
Alex P.: legal expects something they can validate externally (signature chain). currently we only store delete_request_id + evidence_ref, not verification material.
Sam (infra): rotation issue: when we rotate redwood-dsar-keystore every 90d we do not currently persist old public certs in a verifiable form. that makes validating past signatures awkward unless we export and store certs.
Priya R.: storing public key/cert alongside audit entry seems minimal and solves verification. but it's extra retention of crypto metadata — does that violate minimization?
Legal Bot: legal: acceptable to retain public certs/cert metadata for DSAR verification if access is limited and retention matches DSAR lifecycle. public keys are not secret.
Miguel T.: suggested impl: for each DSAR, capture signer_cert_pem (public), signature metadata, SHA256(artifact), delete_request_id in immutable audit entry. redact original PDF, keep evidence_ref encrypted. RBAC restricts read of certs to eng-security + legal.
Sam (infra): RBAC change: introduce role dsar_admin (Okta group) with read-only access to full audit entries (certs + metadata) but no raw-download of artifacts. support role should not get cert access. CR required for group membership.
Priya R.: add alert rule: dsar:kms_key_change when a CMK referenced by any DSAR audit entry is scheduled for rotation/deletion. attach delete_request_id so legal & security get pre-rotation notice.
Alex P.: security check: storing signer_cert_pem — any risk of leaking private material or enabling key reconstruction?
Miguel T.: only storing public cert and signatures + hashes. no private key material. at-rest encryption with CMK + KMS IAM controls. should be fine.
Priya R.: need a DSAR reviewer runbook: steps to validate chain (commands, which certs to fetch, how to check SHA256, who to escalate to). include RBAC test cases.
Sam (infra): will draft CRD for RBAC + alert + audit schema. ETA EOD tomorrow. link here when ready.
Alex P.: decide retention model: cert metadata retained for DSAR_retention_period (legal prefers 7y). evidence_ref encrypted same duration. access logs retained extra 90d. what about purge behavior?
Legal Bot: legal: automated purge okay if there's a logged soft-delete window (recovery X days) and retention policy documented. exceptions via formal retention-exception workflow.
Priya R.: incident triage note: if unauthorized access to DSAR entries detected, escalate to sec-incident (sev2). include delete_request_id in incident timeline and snapshot of access logs.
Miguel T.: will propose retention values in CRD: cert_metadata = 7y, evidence_ref (encrypted) = 7y, access_logs = 7y + 90d. automated purge at expiry with soft-delete 30 days.
Sam (infra): CRD posted: https://crd.internal/redwood/1981234567-dsar-certmeta-rbac-alerts — please review.
Priya R.: left comments on alert thresholds and RBAC acceptance tests.
Alex P.: once CRD ok'd we'll update DSAR runbook + retention-exceptions checklist and sync with legal. thanks everyone.
Legal Bot: legal: acknowledge, will prepare DSAR compliance note and retention confirmation.
Alex P.: closing thread, follow up in CRD review.
